dedupe_keys.name: probabilistic seismic risk assessment of data centre structures with base isolation and server rack anchorage fragility curves and risk matrix

description: This 2020 paper assesses the seismic risk of nonstructural components in data centres, namely server equipment and anchored racks, for a low-rise rigid sample structure in two versions: a conventional fixed-base building and one with a base isolation system. It completes a seismic hazard assessment for the selected site, runs Monte Carlo simulations with uncertainty in structural parameters and in the mechanical properties of the isolation system, generates fragility curves with different methods, and combines them with the site hazard curve to produce risk curves and a proposed risk matrix for data centre design. Base isolation reduces failure probability significantly on higher floors, and code anchorage limits proved more vulnerable than random-vibration limits. Producer: Istanbul Technical University (part of an MSc dissertation), Earthquakes and Structures volume 19, issue 6. Coverage: one sample building and site. Access: abstract and citation on KoreaScience; the full text was not read. Licence and cost: not stated. Caveats: results come from a single sample structure, and no code or fragility tables are available on the page. Simulation uses: it provides a method and reference results for fragility and risk studies of data centres exposed to earthquakes. Related records: none linked.
